sections.heading: Real conditions: si + present
sections.body:
For things that can really happen, use *si* + **present indicative**, and in the result clause the present, future, *ir a*, or a command:

- *Si llueve, no salimos.* (If it rains, we don't go out.)
- *Si tengo tiempo, te llamo / te llamaré / te voy a llamar.*
- *Si ves a Ana, dile que la espero.* (If you see Ana, tell her I'm waiting.)

Never use the present subjunctive after *si*: not *si llueva*.

sections.heading: Hypothetical conditions: si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional
sections.body:
For unlikely or imaginary situations ("if I had…, I would…"), use *si* + **imperfect subjunctive**, and the **conditional** in the result:

- *Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.* (If I had more time, I'd learn to play the guitar.)
- *Si fuera tú, no lo haría.* (If I were you, I wouldn't do it.)
- *¿Qué harías si ganaras la lotería?* (What would you do if you won the lottery?)

The order can be flipped: *Viajaría más si tuviera dinero.* The *si* clause never takes the conditional.

sections.heading: Real or imaginary? You choose
sections.body: The same idea changes meaning with the tense: *Si tengo dinero, voy a viajar* (I might well have it) vs. *Si tuviera dinero, viajaría* (I don't have it — just imagining).

examples: Si llueve, no salimos.
If it rains, we don't go out.
Si tengo tiempo, te llamo.
If I have time, I'll call you.
Si ves a Ana, dile que la espero.
If you see Ana, tell her I'm waiting.
Si estudias, vas a aprobar.
If you study, you're going to pass.
Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.
If I had more time, I'd learn to play the guitar.
Si fuera tú, no lo haría.
If I were you, I wouldn't do it.
¿Qué harías si ganaras la lotería?
What would you do if you won the lottery?
Si ganara la lotería, me mudaría a una isla.
If I won the lottery, I'd move to an island.
Viajaría más si tuviera dinero.
I'd travel more if I had money.
Si pudiera, te ayudaría.
If I could, I'd help you.
Si fuera presidente, cambiaría muchas cosas.
If I were president, I'd change many things.
Si no hiciera tanto frío, iríamos a la playa.
If it weren't so cold, we'd go to the beach.
Si tienes hambre, hay comida en la cocina.
If you're hungry, there's food in the kitchen.
Si tuviéramos tiempo libre, saldríamos más.
If we had free time, we'd go out more.
Si me llamas, voy.
If you call me, I'll come.
Si vivieras aquí, nos veríamos más.
If you lived here, we'd see each other more.
Si supiera la respuesta, te la diría.
If I knew the answer, I'd tell you.

exercises.explain: The *si* clause never takes the conditional.

exercises.prompt: *Si tengo dinero, voy a viajar* suggests…
options: it's quite possible I'll have the money
I definitely don't have the money
I had the money in the past
